editions.briefing: An Iran-blamed drone strike in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians, and Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 12,000 confirmed cases. Nvidia paused server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries over export rules, and X added parental controls for teens. A federal judge ruled the FCC's pressure on ABC licenses violated free speech, and Norse Atlantic suspended all flights. In Idaho, over 60,000 seniors face canceled Medicare Advantage plans.

The Army destroyed nearly five tonnes of explosives in Iowa, calling it a success. Israeli judges urged prosecutors to reconsider Netanyahu's bribery case, and the US announced new tariffs on China, the EU and 12 others. In tech, the FCC cleared SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites. US stocks fell again on AI worries, with Nvidia down 8%. In Idaho, a March trial was set in a fatal Nampa crash.

Huawei was convicted of conspiracy to steal trade secrets but cleared of racketeering, and the US is probing Iran ties to up to 50 hacked ships. Anthropic shares fell below their $83 IPO price, and Nvidia gave back part of its rally. Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $41 billion. In Idaho, a federal scorecard ranks the state first for foster homes per child.

Rep. Jimmy Gomez will resign from Congress after a House Ethics report, and Ukraine says it sank a Russian corvette in Libya. Trump held off an Iowa explosives detonation pending a court ruling. Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, adding nearly $1 trillion in value, and Anthropic launched Claude Ship. The FDA approved the first drug for limb-girdle dystrophy. In Idaho, state revenue is $82.5 million above forecast.

An Army plan to detonate Iowa explosives proceeds despite a court order, and COP31 climate talks collapsed over fossil fuels. President Trump told federal contractors to clear replies to Congress. Google staff joined protests over AI in school search, and Signal limited mobile screenshots. UK energy bills are set to jump in January, and Medicare open enrollment ends Dec. 7. In Idaho, San Diego State upset Boise State 22-20.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, and the FBI is reportedly investigating an apparent hack of its criminal database. An Anthropic staffer claims he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, though the claim has yet to be verified. In business, an Ohio steel mill dropped a plan to cut coal use, and the ICE detention of a Princeton researcher worried international scholars. In Idaho, health officials want a 13% raise for disability caregivers.

COP31 climate talks in Turkey are deadlocked over fossil fuels, and UN talks on killer robots ended without binding rules. Nasdaq fell 10% for the week as the AI boom showed strain, with Anthropic closing near its IPO price. A judge approved a $7.25bn Roundup settlement, and the UK and EU agreed a trade deal. A jury convicted the man behind the Palisades Fire. In Idaho, a state report tied prison growth to drug charges.
